en: The Apadāna of the Elder Asokapūjaka Chapter on the Tamālapupphiya Group, Number Four I am the one who offered a *tamāla* flower to the Buddha, the Fully Enlightened One, the supreme among men. Because of that deed, I have been reborn in heaven for a hundred thousand aeons. For eighty-four thousand aeons, I was a wheel-turning monarch. Having passed away from there, I was reborn in the human world. There, too, I was a king, a lord of the earth, possessing great power and majesty. “In the delightful city of Tivarā,
there was then a royal park;
I was the keeper of that park.”
I was the king’s attendant.
There was one named Paduma by name,
a self-enlightened one (sayambhū) of great splendor.
As he sat upon the white lotus,
the shadow did not leave that Sage.
Seeing the Ashoka tree in full bloom, he said:
I offered a beautiful alms-bowl to the Buddha,
whose name is the Supreme among those with Water-born [Lotus] Marks.
In ninety-four aeons ago,
because I offered that flower,
I have not known a state of misery.
This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha.
For seventy-three aeons,
sixteen [beings] abandoned the passions.
Possessing the seven treasures,
they are wheel-turning monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges—
the Buddha’s instruction has been fulfilled.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Asokapūjaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Āsokapūjaka is the fourth.
